pamphlet_excerpts: Not Think Writing: You might not think that writing programs could cause injuries.
But Fact Injuries: But in fact, injuries from programming have much in common with sports injuries and can be prevented using some of thesame techniques that athletes use.
Main Programming-related: The main programming-related injuries are repetitive stressinjuries, or RSIs.
Athletic Activities RSI: Just as in athletic activities, an RSI occurs whenstress is placed on a joint, pulling on the tendons and musclesaround the joint.
step_by_step_procedure: Stress Happens Repeatedly: When the stress happens repeatedly, the bodydoes not have time to recover and becomes irritated.
Bodyreacts Irritation: The bodyreacts to the irritation by increasing the amount of fluid in thatarea to reduce the stress placed on the tendon or muscle.
Athletes Trained Avoid: And just as athletes are trained to do, you can avoid issues likethe following by developing good habits.
Proper Equipment Preparation: Proper equipment and preparation are the keys to prevention.

pamphlet_excerpts: Theprinting Than Programming: As of theprinting of this merit badge pamphlet, more than 2,500 programming languages have been developed.
New Languages Introduced: By the 1950s and 1960s, many new languages were being introduced, including BASIC, Fortran, and LISP.
Languagestook Programming: These languagestook programming beyond binary and assembly to allowportability of languages beyond just the processor hardware ofthe time.
Programs Written Languages: That is, programs written in these languages could runon two or more kinds of processors or with two or more kindsof operating systems.
step_by_step_procedure: Languages Pascal Werecreated: Many languages, such as Pascal, werecreated to capture new concepts of computer science.
Others Fortran COBOL: Others, such as Fortran and COBOL, were developed to meet specificneeds of science or business.
FORTRAN Formula Translation: FORTRAN (Formula Translation), originally developed in the 1950s, was among the earliest programming languages.
Well-suitedfor Mathematical: Well-suitedfor mathematical calculations, FORTRAN was used mainly forscientific and engineering programming.

pamphlet_excerpts: Value Software Its: The value of software is in its electronically coded instructions, not in the plastic disc or other tangible media upon which theinstructions are stored.
Software Developers Not: Software developers do not sell DVDs orother storage media.
They Actually Sell: What they actually sell is permission touse the programs they have created.
Licensing Renting Bike: Licensing is more like renting a bike than buying one.
step_by_step_procedure: Own Outright Youwant: When you buy a bike, you own it outright and can do what youwant with it.
However Rightto But: When you rent a bike, however, you have the rightto use it, but you may have some restrictions on how long andwhere you can ride it.
Similarly Software Purchase: Similarly, with software, you purchase alicense to use the software in a manner specified by the termsand conditions of the license.
Software Licensed Several: Software may be licensed in several ways, including: Freeware.

requirements.lead_text: Project. With your counselor's guidance, select three different programming languages and development environments. For each subrequirement below, do the following: Write or modify a program using the indicated programming language and development environment. The program must take input and produce output based on computations and decisions made on the input. Debug and demonstrate the program to your counselor. Explain how each program processes inputs, makes decisions based on those inputs, and provides outputs based on computations and decision making.

pamphlet_excerpts: Program Instructions Tells: A program is a set of instructions that tells a processor how to do aparticular task.
Programming Language Tool: A programming language is the tool that converts the programmer’sinstructions into a form the processor can understand.
Roots Modern Programming: The roots of modern programming stretch back to before the first computers.
Programming Languages Their: Most programming languages have their originsin early efforts to automate machines like calculating machines.
step_by_step_procedure: Development Modern: Before the development of modern programming languages, developers used binary code, which is the “native language” of amachine/computer.
Numerals Binary Language: These two numerals used in binary language were numeric codesfor the operations a particular computer could execute (carry out) directly.
Binary Code Allowed: Binary code allowed programmers to turn piecesof computer hardware (circuits) “on” (represented with a 1) or “off” (represented by the numeral 0).
Modern Programminglanguages: All modern programminglanguages are built off the concept of trying to turn humancommands into binary or machine code.

requirements.lead_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include—with your parent or guardian's permission—an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby or healthy lifestyle. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.
